tasks.task: Write or rewrite a landing page for one action

items.when: When a client needs a new page, or a page gets visits but too few sign-ups or sales
Before any writing, to decide where the page should start for this reader
When several ads or buyer groups feed the page, to pick the page type and section order
When the research is in and you need the full page written for one action
When the traffic comes from one ad and the page must pick up where the ad left off
When you want several headlines and openings, each with a reason it fits this reader
When the page is drafted or live, to rank the conversion problems and get fixes

tasks.task: Write homepage, service and about page copy

items.when: When you need a homepage or service page with headline, sections and buttons
When the about page reads like a CV and should tell how and why the business started
When the top of a page is vague, to get five headlines with a subhead, button and proof
When a line could sit on any rival's site, to test it and get a true, picturable rewrite
When the page sounds like the company wrote it and should use the customer's own words

tasks.task: Mine reviews, tickets and calls for customers' own words

items.when: When you have reviews, survey answers, call notes or tickets and need a sorted word bank
When the raw material is long interviews or surveys and you need patterns and buyer types
When you have notes from recent buyers, to map what pushed, pulled and held them back

tasks.task: Plan interviews and surveys to learn why people buy

items.when: When you can talk to five to eight recent buyers and need a script from first thought to use
When a store can ask buyers right after checkout what nearly stopped them
When the answers come back and must be sorted into wants, worries and exact phrases

tasks.task: Write headline and opening options

items.when: Before headlines, to learn what buyers already know and which claims are worn out
When you need options tied to a formula and a reason, not a list of clever lines
When you want more angles on the same promise, without clickbait
When there are several good headlines and a small keyed test should pick the winner

tasks.task: Write a long-form sales page or sales letter

items.when: Before drafting, to sort the research, pick the feeling to write to and outline the letter
When the product sounds like every rival, to find a big idea and a named reason it works
When the outline is agreed and you need the full sales page drafted
Before the body, to pair each doubt the letter must answer with its proof
When the letter reads like a brochure and should sound like one person writing to another
When the draft is done, for a direct-response critique of the weakest parts

tasks.task: Write a welcome, nurture or follow-up email sequence

items.when: When you need a short sequence from new subscriber, enquiry or trial to first purchase
When the list is new and five emails should teach first, then sell, with a review built in
When you want subject lines in several angles for each email to test
Before the sequence is written, to plan three different arcs and draft the first email of each
When a sequence is live with numbers, to see which emails to protect and which to fix

tasks.task: Write launch or promotional emails for one offer

items.when: When there is a launch with a close date and you need the full run of emails planned
When the offer needs a deadline or limit that is real, and the lines to say it
When you need one promotional email written block by block with subject lines
When the email is written and you want subject lines that take different angles
Before the launch emails are written, to compare three runs that differ in promise, proof and timing
When an email is drafted, to get cuts, a pacing map and a ship or fix verdict

tasks.task: Review existing copy and rank what to fix

items.when: When a page, email or ad underperforms and you need ranked problems, rewrites and a test plan
When the copy is sound but loose, to tighten it in set passes for clarity, proof and asks
When the copy leans on pressure, to see which levers are true and which are fake
When the piece is a page and you have screenshots, to score it and rank the fixes
When the copy is well written but starts in the wrong place for what the buyer knows

tasks.task: Map objections and write the FAQ or doubt section

items.when: When people show interest but hesitate, to pair each doubt with the proof that answers it
When you have the list of doubts and need a written answer with proof for each
When you have testimonials and numbers and must choose which to show beside which doubt
When the answers feel too easy, to face the toughest objections and admit real limits
When the promise is big and the reader will not believe it without stronger proof

tasks.task: Sharpen the offer and word the guarantee

items.when: When the copy is fine but the deal is weak or feels risky to the buyer
When the offer needs rebuilding: value, bonuses, guarantee, name and payment terms
When you must pick a guarantee the client can afford, with the refund sums worked out
When the offer has no reason to act now and needs a limit that is true
When the offer is drafted, to score it and get three changes to test first

tasks.task: Check claims, reviews and urgency before copy ships

items.when: Before any copy ships, to catch unproven claims, misleading reviews and false urgency
When you hold the evidence, to see which claims it supports and which go too far
When the copy runs as an ad or feeds one, to flag ad platform policy risks line by line

tasks.task: Plan a copy test and read the result

items.when: When one change is ready to test and you need the cycle from hypothesis to decision
Before a test, to see whether the page has enough visits and how many weeks it needs
When the test has run, to check the split and get a ship or keep call with ranges

tasks.task: Pick a lead magnet and write its opt-in page

items.when: When the client has no free offer yet, to compare ideas and pick the best one
When the magnet is chosen and you need the short signup page written
When the form asks too much, to cut it to what you need and sell the offer
When the opt-in page is drafted, to rank what would stop a visitor signing up

tasks.task: Map a lead funnel from first click to first sale

items.when: When you need the path from page to free offer to emails to sale on one page
When the map is agreed and the emails between sign-up and sale need writing
When a funnel is live, to rank where people drop out and what to test first

tasks.task: Write a quiz funnel with results and follow-ups

items.when: When a quiz should sort people, capture the lead and point each to the right offer
When each quiz result needs its own short follow-up emails
When the quiz needs several titles and opening lines to choose from

tasks.task: Write an advertorial for cold traffic

items.when: Before writing, to rank angles and pick a format for each kind of cold reader
When the angle and facts are set and you need the full piece, labelled as an ad
When the story may turn pitchy too soon, to mark each spot and score it

tasks.task: Write ad copy that matches the page it leads to

items.when: When you need ten different opening lines, each with the line that follows
When the client needs Facebook and Instagram ad text and hooks ready to test
When the ad and page exist, to score how well they match and list the gaps

tasks.task: Write a product page that answers buyers' doubts

items.when: Before writing, to choose the sections that answer this product's main doubts
When the product page works as a sales page for one product and one action
When the product's first screen needs five headlines with a subhead and button
When the page is live, to rank changes to proof, buttons, options and price

tasks.task: Set the value proposition and core message

items.when: When you want several ways to stand apart, each with a statement and a reason
When you need one value proposition built from the offer and customer facts
Before you choose, to read how much buyers know and how tired the market's claims are
When the message is one line, to test whether it is true, specific and easy to picture

tasks.task: Write a comparison, alternative or pricing page

items.when: Before the page, to list the doubts it must answer beside each plan or rival
When buyers search for a rival and you need a fair page that still makes the case
When the page needs several ways to open that do not attack the rival
When the page makes claims about a rival, to check each one against evidence

tasks.task: Script a video sales letter or long video ad

items.when: When the offer needs a seven-part sales video script with hooks and short cuts
When the first fifteen seconds need several openings to choose from
When the script is drafted, to find where it sells too early and tighten it

tasks.task: Gather testimonials and outline a case study

items.when: When the client has happy customers but no quotes, to ask with three easy questions
When you have one customer interview and need a case outline and approval list
When you must decide which proof the pages still lack before you ask for it
Before a quote or result is published, to check it is real, typical and approved

tasks.task: Tighten a draft and match the client's voice

items.when: When the client has no voice rules, to build them from their own documents and calls
When the draft uses long or insider words, to get it back plain with each cut explained
When the copy runs long and must lose a tenth without losing the point
When the draft is close, for set passes on clarity, voice, proof and calls to action

always.when: At the start of a new client, to build a research doc, buyer sheet and offer brief to reuse
Before any copy goes to the client, to fix each line that sounds machine-written
When the copy states a number or fact you cannot trace to the client's own material
Before delivery, to catch typos and product names spelt two ways

helpers.when: When the test needs tracking set up, traffic split or results read from analytics
When the job needs real interviews or a survey run, not only mining what exists
When the emails must be built as flows with segments, timing and inbox checks
When the page needs layout, images and a build, not only the words
When the job is a full ad campaign across formats, not ads for one page
When the weak point is the price or the plan structure, not how it is worded

gaps: No library item writes a thank-you or confirmation page that sets up the next step after sign-up or purchase
No library item writes pricing page copy: plan names, who each plan is for and the lines beside each price
No library item checks a quiz funnel's questions and result pages before launch, or offers different quiz concepts
No library item gives clearly different openings for a video sales letter; only the kit's headline prompt covers it
No library item writes a full customer case study from interview notes; the library stops at an outline
No library item scores reading level for sales copy and marks the lines that are too hard
No library item writes webinar registration page copy or a webinar pitch script
No library item writes checkout and order form copy: trust lines, order summary and button words
No library item offers different whole-page concepts for a homepage or service page; only headline options exist
The 70-item limit left out good fits: comment mining, cart and win-back email copy, popups and comparison tables
